title: kell + Infinitive: What You Must Do

sections.title: From "X is needed" to "you must do X"
sections.content: You already know kell with a noun: Kell még valami? ("Is anything else needed?"). kell also combines with an infinitive (a verb ending in -ni) to say what must be done — and just like with a noun, kell itself never changes for person: Be kell csekkolni ("[One] must check in") stays kell no matter who has to do it. Who's doing it is understood from context, or can be added with -nak/-nek: Nekem be kell csekkolnom.

sections.title: kell + infinitive
rows: you have to show your passport
you have to fill out a form

items.english: At the airport, you have to check in.

items.spanish: A kapunál meg kell mutatni az útlevelet.
items.english: At the gate, you have to show your passport.

sections.content: The infinitive always goes right before kell, and any short prefix on the verb (be-, meg-, ki-) splits off and moves to the very front of the sentence: be kell csekkolni, not becsekkolni kell.
